text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan survives parliament questioning. The minister was grilled for almost 12 hours on Tuesday over alleged irregularities in key financial bodies which he heads.

- In an unprecedented move against Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates semi-official newspaper al-Ittihad said Iraq's ban from the Pan Arab Games in Lebanon is "far from Arab, Moslem and human politeness...and is shameful".
- Iraqi message to Kuwait: A child choked to death in Cairo. A four-year-old Kuwaiti child was found dead in his hotel room in Cairo with a note saying the killing was a message from Iraq.
- Saudi Arabia mediates between non-Arab Iran and the UAE to resolve a dispute over three Gulf islands. Gulf Arab states describe Iranian presence on the islands as an "occupation".

- Sudan's President Omar Hassan al-Bashir says Khartoum is working to normalise relations with Kuwait which downgraded diplomatic ties with several Arab states for siding with former occupier Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.

- Royal Jordanian Airlines says Kuwait extended all required services to its first flight to the Gulf state since the 1990 Iraqi invasion. The national carriers of the two Arab states resumed direct air links earlier this month.

- Washington steps in to stop Kuwait's gun deal with China. The United States on Tuesday urged Kuwait to reject the Chinese self-propelled howitzers and "buy American". Kuwait's main 1991 Gulf War allies Washington and London are both seeking to win the deal with the U.S. M109 A6 Paladin and the British AS90.
